chapters.name: Key Ideas and Details
chapters.summary: Finding the main idea, identifying supporting details, and drawing inferences that the passage supports.
keyPoints: The main idea covers the whole passage, not just one detail.
An inference must be supported by the text, not by outside opinions.
Questions often ask what the author implies or what the passage suggests.

chapters.name: Craft, Structure, and Language Skills
chapters.summary: The author's tone and purpose, how a passage is organized, word meaning in context, and telling facts from opinions.
keyPoints: Use the sentences around a word to find its meaning in context.
A fact can be checked; an opinion states a belief or judgment.
Look at transition words to see how ideas are related.

chapters.name: Integration of Knowledge and Ideas
chapters.summary: Reading charts and graphs with text, evaluating arguments and evidence, and comparing two related passages.
keyPoints: Check whether the evidence really supports the claim.
When two passages are paired, find where the authors agree and where they differ.
Read the labels and units on a chart before answering.

chapters.name: Grammar and Usage
chapters.summary: Finding errors in subject-verb agreement, pronouns, verb tense, modifiers, word choice, and idioms.
keyPoints: A verb must agree with its subject, even when other words come between them.
A pronoun must clearly refer to one noun and agree with it in number.
Some usage questions have no error, so do not force a change.

chapters.name: Sentence Correction and Mechanics
chapters.summary: Choosing the best version of a sentence: fixing run-ons, fragments, comma errors, parallel structure, and misplaced modifiers.
keyPoints: Two complete sentences need a period, a semicolon, or a comma plus a conjunction.
Items in a list should have the same grammatical form.
The best answer is correct, clear, and not wordy.

chapters.name: Revision in Context
chapters.summary: Improving a draft: choosing transitions, combining sentences, adding or removing sentences, and keeping a consistent focus and tone.
keyPoints: A transition must match the relationship between the ideas.
Remove sentences that do not support the paragraph's main point.
Keep the tone and style of the rest of the passage.

chapters.name: Research Skills
chapters.summary: Judging the credibility and relevance of sources and recognizing the parts of a citation.
keyPoints: A credible source has a qualified author, is current enough, and shows its evidence.
A primary source is a firsthand record; a secondary source explains or interprets it.
Know the parts of a citation: author, title, publisher or journal, date, and pages.

chapters.name: Number and Quantity
chapters.summary: Integers, fractions, decimals, place value, ratio and proportion, percent, rates, and units of measurement.
keyPoints: To find a percent of a number, change the percent to a decimal and multiply.
Set up a proportion as two equal ratios and cross-multiply.
Convert units before you add or compare measurements.

chapters.name: Algebra
chapters.summary: Writing and evaluating expressions, solving linear equations and inequalities, and solving word problems with algebra.
keyPoints: Do the same operation to both sides of an equation.
When you multiply or divide an inequality by a negative number, flip the sign.
Check a solution by putting it back into the original equation.

chapters.name: Geometry
chapters.summary: Properties of shapes and angles, congruence and similarity, the Pythagorean theorem, and perimeter, area, and volume.
keyPoints: The angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Similar figures have equal angles and proportional sides.
Area uses square units; volume uses cubic units.

chapters.name: Data Interpretation, Statistics, and Probability
chapters.summary: Reading tables and graphs, finding mean, median, mode, and range, and finding simple probabilities.
keyPoints: The median is the middle value after the data are put in order.
An outlier changes the mean much more than the median.
Probability = favorable outcomes divided by all equally likely outcomes.
